titulo: Nouns and articles: Der, die, das

aula.objetivo: Use der, die, das and ein/eine/kein, capitalize nouns and form the most common plurals.

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you learn every noun together with its article and plural, spot gender from clues, and use ein/eine and der/die/das — even though English gets by with just "the" and "a".

blocos.contexto: Jonas shows Camila around the shared apartment.

linhas.ru: — Hier ist das Zimmer. Da ist ein Bett und dort ist ein Tisch.
linhas.pt: — Here's the room. There's a bed there, and a table over there.
linhas.audio: Hier ist das Zimmer. Da ist ein Bett und dort ist ein Tisch.

linhas.ru: — Wie schön! Ist das eine Lampe?
linhas.pt: — How nice! Is that a lamp?
linhas.audio: Wie schön! Ist das eine Lampe?

linhas.ru: — Ja, das ist die Lampe. Und da ist das Fenster. Es ist groß.
linhas.pt: — Yes, that's the lamp. And there's the window. It's big.
linhas.audio: Ja, das ist die Lampe. Und da ist das Fenster. Es ist groß.

linhas.ru: — Der Schrank ist dort. Er ist neu.
linhas.pt: — The wardrobe is over there. It's new.
linhas.audio: Der Schrank ist dort. Er ist neu.

linhas.ru: — Sie ist hier. Die Stühle sind alt, aber der Tisch ist neu.
linhas.pt: — It's here. The chairs are old, but the table is new.
linhas.audio: Sie ist hier. Die Stühle sind alt, aber der Tisch ist neu.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: English has one word for "the". German has three, one per gender: der (masculine), die (feminine) and das (neuter). In the plural, it's always die. STEP 2: English calls every object "it". German doesn't: a thing is «er», «sie» or «es» depending on its gender — «Der Tisch ist neu. Er ist modern.» STEP 3: so never learn Tisch. Learn der Tisch.
blocos.comparacao: Old English had genders too — modern English dropped them, German kept them. That's why the gender of a German noun can't be guessed from its meaning: a table is masculine, a lamp feminine, a girl («das Mädchen») neuter. The gender is part of the word, and the only safe way is to learn it together with the word, as one unit.

blocos.titulo: Der, die, das: the three genders
blocos.explicacao: In German every noun has a gender: masculine (der), feminine (die) or neuter (das). Gender is grammar, not meaning: «das Mädchen» (the girl) is neuter. So always memorize the article with the word. EVERY noun is written with a CAPITAL letter, anywhere in the sentence — not just names, as in English. Endings give clues, with exceptions: -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -tion, -ie and most words in -e are feminine; -er, -ling and -ismus are masculine; -chen, -lein, -um and -ment are neuter. Days of the week, months and seasons are masculine. Handy English link: -heit and -schaft often match English -hood and -ship (die Kindheit = childhood, die Freundschaft = friendship).
blocos.comparacao: English only keeps gender in he/she/it for people and animals. German assigns a gender to every noun, and it rarely matches what you'd expect: «das Kind» (the child) is neuter, «die Person» is feminine even for a man.

linhas.exemplo: der Mann, der Tisch, der Vater
die Frau, die Lampe, die Mutter
das Kind, das Buch, das Haus
die Zeitung, die Freiheit, die Nation, die Familie, die Lampe
das Mädchen, das Museum, das Dokument
der Montag, der Juli, der Sommer

erros.motivo: Kind is neuter, and nouns are capitalized.

blocos.enunciado: Say the article and the word out loud: «der Mann, die Frau, das Kind, der Tisch, die Lampe, das Buch».
